chunks: And among what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Sinān, from Abū al-Jārūd, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: When should I perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness? He said: Before the taslīm, for when you give the taslīm, the sanctity of your salat has departed.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as a kind of taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrines of many of the ʿāmmah. And Abū Jaʿfar Ibn Bābawayh al-Qummī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I give fatwa according to them in a state of taqiyyah.

key_terms.أُفْتِي: I issue a legal ruling or fatwa
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the concluding salutation that ends the salat
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precaution in expressing a ruling under sensitive circumstances
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general body of non-Shia Muslims in this polemical legal context
key_terms.حُرْمَةُ صَلَاتِكَ: the inviolable sanctity and formal state of the prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in salat

ai.seo_question: When are the two sajdahs of forgetfulness performed, and how do Shia scholars understand reports placing them before the taslīm?
ai.summary: This report discusses the timing of the two sajdahs of forgetfulness in salat, stating that they are performed before the taslīm. The compiler then explains that this report is understood in Shia scholarly tradition as issued under taqiyyah because it conforms to the views of many among the ʿāmmah, and Ibn Bābawayh states that he gives fatwa by it in situations of taqiyyah.
